questions.q: What problem are Smart View Report Packages designed to solve?
options: Letting one person work entirely alone on a single workbook
Giving multiple contributors a secure, structured, auditable way to jointly author, review, and sign off on one collaborative report
Replacing the need for the GL balances cube
Scheduling a BI Publisher report to run nightly
questions.explain: Report Packages coordinate multiple contributors toward one finished, consistently formatted, properly reviewed deliverable, with a recorded approval trail.

questions.q: What are the three possible development phases of a Report Package?
options: Design, build, deploy
Filter, prompt, schedule
Author, review, sign-off
Data model, template, report
questions.explain: A Report Package's development can include an author phase, a review phase, and a sign-off phase, though not every package needs all three.

questions.q: In the review phase of a Report Package, what is the typical role of a reviewer?
options: Reviewers rewrite the entire document from scratch
Reviewers have no access to the package at all
Reviewers automatically approve everything without reading it
Reviewers examine content and leave comments on their assigned areas, without necessarily having edit rights to the content itself
questions.explain: The review phase lets stakeholders provide feedback via comments on their assigned areas, distinct from the authors who actually edit the content.

questions.q: Which type of Report Package is reviewed directly using Smart View?
options: PDF-based packages
Neither type uses Smart View for review
Only packages with no review phase configured
Word- or PowerPoint-based packages
questions.explain: Word- and PowerPoint-based packages can be reviewed directly in Smart View; PDF-based packages are reviewed through the Narrative Reporting web interface instead.

questions.q: What happens during the sign-off phase of a Report Package?
options: Content is drafted for the first time
The package is permanently deleted
Designated approvers formally approve the content, creating a recorded trail before publication or distribution
Reviewers are assigned to their sections for the first time
questions.explain: Sign-off creates a formal, recorded approval trail, which is part of why Report Packages suit regulatory or board-level deliverables.
